title: Reconstruction from invariant coefficients and a common retraction
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings and let $\sigma,\tau:A\to B$ and $\varepsilon:B\to A$ be unital ring homomorphisms satisfying $\varepsilon\sigma=\varepsilon\tau=\mathrm{id}_A$. Put $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$, with its subring structure and inclusion into $A$. Let $r\geq1$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in A$ such that every $b\in B$ has a unique expansion $b=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$ with $a_j\in A$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Assume additionally that for every $a\in A$ the coefficients in this expansion of $\tau(a)$ all belong to $C$. Then $(x_j)_{j=1}^r$ is a $C$-basis of $A$. The ring homomorphism $\phi:A\otimes_C A\to B$ specified by $\phi(a\otimes a_2)=\sigma(a)\tau(a_2)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. With the $A$-module structure on the first tensor factor, $(1\otimes x_j)_{j=1}^r$ is an $A$-basis of $A\otimes_C A$, and $\phi(1\otimes x_j)=\tau(x_j)$ for every $j$.

proof.text: For $a\in A$, write $\tau(a)=\sum_j\sigma(c_j)\tau(x_j)$ with $c_j\in C$ by hypothesis. Applying $\varepsilon$ gives $a=\sum_jc_jx_j$. If $\sum_jd_jx_j=0$ with $d_j\in C$, applying $\tau$ and using $\tau(d_j)=\sigma(d_j)$ gives $\sum_j\sigma(d_j)\tau(x_j)=0$. Uniqueness of the assumed expansion in $B$, compared with the zero coefficient tuple, gives $d_j=0$ in $A$, hence in its subring $C$. Subtracting any two expansions proves uniqueness. Thus the $x_j$ form a $C$-basis by [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] to the inclusion $C\to A$ and the $C$-module $A$ with the basis just proved. It gives the $A$-basis $e_j=1\otimes x_j$ of $T=A\otimes_C A$, with $A$ acting on the first factor. There is no nontriviality, flatness, or field hypothesis in this base-change result.

proof.text: The equalizer $C$ is closed under addition, negatives, multiplication and the unit since $\sigma,\tau$ preserve these operations. Give $B$ its $C$-algebra structure by their common restriction. Both maps are then $C$-algebra homomorphisms. The tensor pushout property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives the unital ring map $\phi:T\to B$ with $\phi(a\otimes a_2)=\sigma(a)\tau(a_2)$. In particular $\phi(e_j)=\tau(x_j)$; also $\phi(a\otimes1)=\sigma(a)$, so multiplicativity makes $\phi$ $A$-linear for the specified actions.

proof.text: For any $b\in B$, its given expansion $b=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$ equals $\phi(\sum_j a_je_j)$, proving surjectivity. If $\phi(z)=0$, expand $z=\sum_j a_je_j$ in the basis from step 2. Then $0=\sum_j\sigma(a_j)\tau(x_j)$, so uniqueness of the expansion of zero in $B$ forces every $a_j=0$, and $z=0$. Additivity now gives injectivity by applying this to a difference. The inverse of this bijective unital ring homomorphism preserves addition, multiplication and the unit by applying $\phi$ and cancelling it. Thus $\phi$ is a ring isomorphism with all the specified basis images.
